subject: On-prem connectivity acceptance: next steps and checklist
messages:
From: Aaron Mills <aaron.mills@acmecorp.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: net-owners@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 4 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Connectivity acceptance criteria for Acme on-prem deployment

Dylan / Redwood team —

Thanks for the architecture walkthrough last week. We've pulled together a short list of items our infrastructure team needs to close before we can sign off on the private deployment connection (control plane <-> data plane). High level asks:

- Confirmation of control-plane egress destinations and port ranges (for firewall rules).
- Expected BGP or static routing config for the edge router(s).
- Proof of tenant isolation (per-tenant routing/VRF or equivalent).
- A short runbook for failover (if the primary edge fails).
- Network diagram that shows NAT/Egress, proxies, and MTLS termination points.

Can you respond with a one-page acceptance checklist and any reference diagrams we can drop into our change request? We are aiming to start the scheduled cutover on Friday, so a short readout today/tomorrow would be great.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Aaron
Network Ops | Acme Corp

---
Attachment: acme_connectivity_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Aaron Mills <aaron.mills@acmecorp.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Dec 2028 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Connectivity acceptance criteria for Acme on-prem deployment

Aaron —

Thanks for the clear list. We're aligned and have drafted a compact acceptance pack below and attached two artifacts: a one-page checklist (vpc-acceptance-checklist.pdf) and the reference diagram (private_vpc_reference_v1.svg). Also attached is a mapping matrix that ties Acme firewall rules to Redwood service endpoints (acme_connectivity_matrix_v1.xlsx).

Quick summary answers to your bullets:

- Control-plane egress: 52.44.12.0/24 and 52.44.13.0/24 on TCP 443 outbound. We use mTLS to the control endpoint; port 443 only.
- Edge routing: we prefer EBGP with the following ASNs (Acme: 65012, Redwood-edge: 65421). If you must use static routes, advertise 10.240.0.0/16 via the peer IP configured in the matrix.
- Tenant isolation: per-tenant VRF + VNI segmentation. Control-plane requests carry tenant id headers and are enforced by the edge proxy (policy reference included in the drive link).
- Failover: attached runbook (page 2 of the checklist) — primary edge healthcheck, BGP failover timers (30s), and automated reroute to warm-burst capacity.
- Diagrams: private_vpc_reference_v1.svg shows the demarc, edge NAT, control-plane egress, and operator console paths.

Next steps I propose:
1) You drop the attached checklist into your change request.
2) Neha (cc'd) will follow up with the exact BGP session parameters and a short test plan for validation.
3) Jasmine will schedule a 30-min verification slot with your network team tomorrow morning.

If that plan looks good I'll mark it as "Ready for CR" and we can proceed to cutover as scheduled.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Platform Ops Engineer | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — private deployment team

Attachments: vpc-acceptance-checklist.pdf (pdf, 12KB); private_vpc_reference_v1.svg (svg, 140KB)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Aaron Mills <aaron.mills@acmecorp.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Dec 2028 13:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Connectivity acceptance criteria for Acme on-prem deployment

Aaron — quick technical addendum to Dylan's note:

- BGP params: local-as 65421, remote-as 65012, hold-time 90s, keepalive 30s. Peer IPs: see acme_connectivity_matrix_v1.xlsx (sheet: BGP).
- Backend service CIDRs (for data-plane): 10.241.0.0/18 (runtime pods), 10.241.64.0/18 (cache subsystem). Advertise only 10.241.0.0/16 to avoid leaking internal segments — per guidance in the matrix.
- MTLS endpoints: control-plane certificate rotation is every 7 days by default (can extend for enterprise to 30 days with KMS integration).

Test plan (short):
- Step 1: BGP session establishment and AS path validation (10 min).
- Step 2: Control-plane handshake over mTLS; verify certificate chain and tenant header enforcement (15 min).
- Step 3: Data-plane echo test to a staging tenant IP and verify routing path and NAT behavior (10 min).

I'll be on the verification call and can provide the exact commands for BGP/MTLS checks.

-Neha
Senior Network Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Mills <aaron.mills@acmecorp.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: net-owners@acmecorp.com
Date: Tue, 5 Dec 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Connectivity acceptance criteria for Acme on-prem deployment

Dylan / Neha / Jasmine —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We reviewed the checklist and ran a quick validation against our staging edge. Confirming the following and clearing this for our CR: 

- Firewall changes: opened outbound TCP 443 to 52.44.12.0/24 & 52.44.13.0/24; rules validated.
- BGP: session established to Redwood-edge with ASNs as provided. Hold/keepalive values applied.
- MTLS: control-plane handshake succeeded; tenant-id header present and validated in the staging trace.
- Isolation: VRF boundaries are in place; we observed no leaked routes during the test.

We have one small ask: can Redwood provide the explicit probe target IP and port for canary healthchecks (so we can include it in the CR ticket)? Also a brief note on expected failover RTO for our change notes (we measured 35s in the staging test).

If you can drop those two items into the checklist I'll attach it and mark the CR as approved for the Friday cutover.

We'll plan to join the verification slot tomorrow AM — thanks again.

Aaron
Network Ops | Acme Corp
